title: Polynomial comparison model and normalization of algebraic diagonal classes
statement: Let $R\to A$ be a flat finitely presented homomorphism of commutative Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], [def-weil-pbc-finitely-presented-algebra], [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Work in the ordinary module derived categories $D(A),D(B)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], using derived tensor products computed by flat resolutions and derived Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] on the one-point ringed site. Put $B=A\otimes_R A$, $p_1(a)=a\otimes1$, and make $A$ a $B$-module by multiplication $\delta:B\to A$ [def-trf-affine-diagonal-module-data]. Choose a polynomial presentation $P=R[x_1,\ldots,x_n]\twoheadrightarrow A$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] and set $C=R\operatorname{Hom}_P(A,P)[n]\in D(A)$ with its derived-coinduction $A$-action [def-trf-derived-coinduction]. For $T\in D(A)$ write $T_1=T\otimes_{A,p_1}^{\mathbf L}B$. Then $C$ is pseudo-coherent over $A$ [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex], has finite Tor amplitude over $R$, and $R\operatorname{Hom}_B(A,C_1)\cong A$ in $D(B)$. Let $M,N\in D(A)$ be pseudo-coherent, each with finite Tor amplitude over $R$, and let $\gamma:A\to M_1$ and $\theta:A\to N_1$ be morphisms in $D(B)$ for which multiplication gives isomorphisms $A\to R\operatorname{Hom}_B(A,M_1)$ and $A\to R\operatorname{Hom}_B(A,N_1)$. Here finite $R$-Tor amplitude means that for each such $T$ there are integers $a_T\le b_T$ with $H^i(T\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}Q)=0$ for every $R$-module $Q$ and $i\notin[a_T,b_T]$. Multiplication by a class is the transpose of the derived multiplication of the diagonal algebra followed by that class. There are isomorphisms $M\cong C\cong N$ in $D(A)$, and the scalar maps $A\to R\operatorname{Hom}_A(T,T)$ for $T=M,N$ are isomorphisms. The groups $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B)}(A,M_1)$ and $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B)}(A,N_1)$ are free rank-one $A$-modules with bases $\gamma$ and $\theta$. There is exactly one isomorphism $a:M\to N$ with $(a\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{A,p_1}B)\gamma=\theta$. Moreover $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A)}(T,T[i])=0$ for $T=M,N$ and every $i<0$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-algebraic-shriek-relative-perfect] to the chosen polynomial presentation: a finitely presented algebra is finite type. Its object $K$ is exactly $C$ with the specified coinduction action. Thus $C$ is pseudo-coherent, has finite $R$-Tor amplitude, and its scalar map $A\to R\operatorname{Hom}_A(C,C)$ is an isomorphism.

Put $p_2(a)=1\otimes a$. If $x_j$ generate $A/R$, then $x_j\otimes1$ generate $B$ over $p_2(A)$, so [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] makes $B$ Noetherian. Write $\varphi:R\to A$. Flat base change (iii) of [lem-trf-algebraic-shriek-calculus], with base map $\varphi$ and input $R[0]$, gives $C_1\cong p_2^!(A[0])$ in $D(B)$; the original algebra factor is the first tensor factor. The multiplication $\delta:B\twoheadrightarrow A$ is a finite-type map and $\delta p_2=1_A$. Parts (i)--(ii) of that same node give $\delta^!p_2^!(A[0])\cong A[0]$ in $D(A)$, since the input is bounded below. Part (i) identifies $\delta^!$ with derived coinduction along the surjection $\delta$. By [lem-trf-derived-coinduction-adjunction], restricting $\delta^!C_1$ along $\delta$ gives $R\operatorname{Hom}_B(A,C_1)$. Restricting the displayed isomorphism therefore gives the required isomorphism with the diagonal module $A$ in $D(B)$.

proof.text: The hypotheses on $M,N$ and steps 1--2 put each of the pairs $(M,C)$ and $(C,N)$ under [lem-trf-algebraic-relative-dualizing-isomorphism]. Hence $M\cong C\cong N$. For $T=M,N$ choose an isomorphism $b:T\to C$. Conjugation $f\mapsto bfb^{-1}$ identifies the derived endomorphism objects by functoriality of [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]; it sends $r\,1_T$ to $r\,1_C$ for every $r\in A$, since $b$ is $A$-linear. It consequently identifies the scalar map for $T$ with that for $C$. The latter is invertible by step 1, proving the claimed scalar-map isomorphisms.

source.place: Tag 0E2D, lemma-uniqueness-relative-dualizing; Tag 0BZW, scalar endomorphisms. Conjugation is the elementary naturality argument.

proof.text: On the one-point ringed site global sections are the identity. A shift of a K-injective complex is K-injective: shift an acyclic source in its defining null-homotopy test. Apply [lem-pur-rhom-into-kinjective-local] to a representative $L$ and a K-injective representative $I$ of $U[i]$. Degree-zero Hom cocycles modulo boundaries are derived morphisms. Since $\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(L,I_U[i])=\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(L,I_U)[i]$ (both differentials are $(-1)^i d_{I_U}f-(-1)^j f d_L$ in degree $j$), [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] gives $H^iR\operatorname{Hom}(L,U)=\operatorname{Hom}_{D}(L,U[i])$. In particular step 3 gives $\operatorname{End}_{D(A)}(T)=A$, with $r$ acting as $r1_T$, and $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A)}(T,T[i])=0$ for $i<0$.

source.place: Tag 0A94, lemma-RHom-into-K-injective; shift formula on the Hom complex. Tag 08JA, lemma-section-RHom-over-U, is the corresponding derived-Hom formulation.

proof.text: Apply the degree-zero identification of step 4 over $B$ to the given isomorphism $m_\gamma:A\to R\operatorname{Hom}_B(A,M_1)$. Its map on $H^0$ is $A\to\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B)}(A,M_1)$, $r\mapsto r\gamma$: under transpose, evaluation at the derived unit gives $m_\gamma(1)=\gamma$, because multiplication by $1$ on the diagonal algebra is the identity. The same calculation applies to $\theta$. The identifications are $A$-linear: precomposing by multiplication by $r$ on $A$ equals postcomposing by multiplication by $p_1(r)$ on the target, by $B$-linearity. Thus these two Hom modules are free on $\gamma$ and $\theta$.

source.place: Tag 0E2W, lemma-uniqueness-relative-dualizing, paragraph beginning Suppose we have an isomorphism; unit calculation from the stated multiplication transpose.

proof.text: Choose an isomorphism $b:M\to N$ from step 3. Postcomposition by $b_1=b\otimes_{A,p_1}^{\mathbf L}B$ is an $A$-linear bijection between the two Hom modules. Write $b_1\gamma=u\theta$ and $(b_1^{-1})\theta=v\gamma$. Substitution and the basis property give $uv=vu=1$. Then $a=u^{-1}b$ is an isomorphism and $a_1\gamma=\theta$. If $a\prime$ is another such isomorphism, step 4 says $a\prime a^{-1}=s1_N$ for a unique $s\in A$. Its action on $\theta$ is $s\theta=\theta$, so the basis property forces $s=1$ and $a\prime=a$. This proves existence and uniqueness without choosing an orientation of $C$.
